name:
An object that connects two quantities for a fixed odd n: the least modulus r
congruent to 3 modulo 4 at which the primes of n(n+r)/4 generate -1 in the units
modulo r with exponents available inside the square, and the fourth root of n.
The object must express the constant relating them, must express what makes the
constant large, and must be stated so that a proof of the connection would bound
the first quantity by a function of n.

phase_0.boundary_condition: The system is bounded by the fixed odd integer n and the congruence condition r ≡ 3 (mod 4), which together define the domain of admissible moduli and the scope of the constant relating the least modulus to the fourth root of n.

VINIT.chosen_element: The uninitialized state before any modulus r or fourth root of n is named or computed.
VINIT.justification: Before the system begins, no modulus has been selected, no prime has been evaluated, and no constant has been derived. This is the void from which the entire construction emerges.

TANCH.chosen_element: The terminal anchor is the bound that relates the least modulus r to a function of n, closing the system within a provable inequality.
TANCH.justification: The system is contained by the requirement that a proof must bound the first quantity (least modulus r) by a function of n. This boundary enforces closure and prevents unbounded divergence.

AFWD.chosen_element: The forward morphism is the derivation of the constant from the fourth root of n and the primes of n(n+r)/4.
AFWD.justification: The constant is constructed by advancing from the fourth root of n through the primes of n(n+r)/4, generating -1 in the units modulo r. This is a directed transformation toward the target quantity.

AREV.chosen_element: The reverse morphism is the descent from the constant back to the structural relationship between r and n.
AREV.justification: The constant's magnitude is determined by reversing the direction of analysis, tracing back from the catalytic effect of the fourth root of n to the modulus r and its congruence class.

CLINK.chosen_element: Composition chains the evaluation of primes, the computation of the fourth root, and the derivation of the constant into a single sequential process.
CLINK.justification: Each step depends on the previous: primes are evaluated, the fourth root is computed, and the constant is derived. These morphisms are composed in sequence to form the full construction.

IMSCRIB.chosen_element: Self-reference occurs when the constant, once derived, is used to re-evaluate the relationship between r and n, forming a closed loop of mutual determination.
IMSCRIB.justification: The constant is not external to the system; it is defined by and defines the relationship between the least modulus and the fourth root of n. This self-recognition is the identity of the object.

FSPLIT.chosen_element: The system splits into two branches: one evaluating the primes of n(n+r)/4 generating -1 in units modulo r, and the other computing the fourth root of n.
FSPLIT.justification: The two quantities — the least modulus r and the fourth root of n — are distinct and must be evaluated independently before their relationship can be established. The split separates the modulus-based computation from the root-based computation.

FFUSE.chosen_element: The two branches rejoin into the single constant that relates the least modulus r to the fourth root of n.
FFUSE.justification: The constant is the unified result of both branches: it captures how the primes of n(n+r)/4 and the fourth root of n interact. The arms rejoin to form this constant, which may hold both affirmative and negative information (B-state) if the relationship is contradictory.

EVALT.chosen_element: The affirmative state is the successful derivation of the constant from the primes of n(n+r)/4 and the fourth root of n.
EVALT.justification: When the primes generate -1 in the units modulo r and the fourth root of n is correctly computed, the constant is affirmatively established.

EVALF.chosen_element: The negative state is the failure to derive the constant, either because the primes do not generate -1 or the fourth root is undefined.
EVALF.justification: If the primes of n(n+r)/4 do not generate -1 in the units modulo r, or if the fourth root of n cannot be computed, the constant cannot be derived, resulting in a refuted state.

ENGAGR.chosen_element: The paradice state holds both the affirmation and negation of the constant's derivation simultaneously.
ENGAGR.justification: In cases where the primes generate -1 and the fourth root exists, but the constant's magnitude is ambiguous or contradictory, both states are held without resolution. This is the B-state of the system.

IFIX.chosen_element: The permanent record of the constant and its relationship to n and r is fixed in an append-only register.
IFIX.justification: Once the constant is derived, it is irreversibly recorded as a fixed point in the system. This record cannot be undone and serves as the basis for bounding the least modulus r by a function of n.

phase_3.void_description: No modulus r has been selected, no primes have been evaluated, and no constant has been derived. The system is uninitialized.
phase_3.true_description: The constant has been successfully derived from the primes of n(n+r)/4 and the fourth root of n, and the relationship between r and n is affirmatively established.
phase_3.false_description: The constant cannot be derived because the primes do not generate -1 in the units modulo r, or the fourth root of n is undefined.
phase_3.both_description: The constant is derived but its magnitude is ambiguous or contradictory, holding both the affirmation and negation of the relationship between r and n simultaneously.
